translation_notes: best fit of the seven: the three self.graph.add() calls, the two term constructors and the three namespace accesses collapse into one four-line g{ } island. `bnode = BNode()` is used exactly once, as an object carrying two properties, so it is absorbed into an inline [ ... ] property list and the variable disappears -- the textbook case for the notation.
ns_rdf['type'] -> a ; ns_rdfa['context'] -> rdfa:context ; ns_ht['Response'] -> ht:Response ; the `ns_ht = Namespace(...)` line is absorbed by `@prefix ht: <http://www.w3.org/2006/http#> .`.

URIRef('http://www.w3.org/2006/http#%s' % http_code) -> ht:{http_code}, a prefixed name with an interpolated local part. f<http://www.w3.org/2006/http#{http_code}> transpiles to the same IRI and is textually closer to the original, but the prefix is already declared so the pname form is more idiomatic. Note the local part then starts with a digit ('404'), which Turtle's PN_LOCAL allows and the transpiler accepts.

the rdflib imports (URIRef, BNode, Namespace, RDF as ns_rdf) all become dead once the notation absorbs the term constructors, so they are dropped in translated.ldpy; the `from pyrdfa_ns import ns_xsd, ns_distill, ns_rdfa` line is kept as-is because ns_xsd and ns_distill were already unused in the extracted region.

context shim: `from . import ns_xsd, ns_distill, ns_rdfa` -> local pyrdfa_ns.py, copied verbatim from pyRdfa/__init__.py of the same commit. The corpus checkout could not be put on sys.path because it vendors a whole old rdflib package that would shadow the installed one.

restored context: the extracted region uses `ns_rdf` and `Namespace`, which the extraction dropped; the corresponding import lines from options.py (lines 20-28 upstream) are added to original.py. Identical for both representations, and both are gone from translated.ldpy since the notation no longer needs them.

the driver stands in for the ProcessorGraph instance with a minimal object whose __eq__ compares self.graph by isomorphism; a negative control (a different HTTP code) was checked to confirm the comparison really discriminates.
